full_judgment:
3. Plaintiffs sought above stated reliefs pressing into service contentions that Ram Nath Mondol had been owner of Suit property. Ram Nath Mondal drew his last breath leaving behind three sons, Mon Mohan Mondal, Ovi-monue Mondal and Kailash Mondal. In Cadastral Survey record-of-right name of Mon Mohan Mondal and Ovimonue Mondal had been recorded in equal share and Kailash Mondal having been a minor during Cadastral Survey Settlement Operation period his name was not recorded in Cadastral Survey record-of-right, Cadastral Survey period of Right was wrong. Ovimonue Mondal breathed his last leaving behind two brohers Mon Mohan Mondal and Kailash Mondal. Kailash Mondal being owner to the extent of 8 annas share of cadastral surevy Khatian died leaving behind two sons, Hemanta Mondal and Neekunja Mondal. Neekunja Mondal died leaving behind first-fifth plaintiffs. Hemanta Mondal died leaving two sons, Deen Nath Mondal and Personath Mondal, Deen Nath Mondal faced death leaving behind fourth-defendant. Parsonath Mondal died leaving three sons, fifth-seventh defendants. Plaintiffs are successors of Neekanja Mondal. Plaintiffs demanded partition from co-sharer defendnats and that demand of partition had been turned down by first-Seventh defendants taking stand that plaintiffs got no title on Suit property. Cloud had been cast upon right and title of plaintiffs over suit property. Plaintiffs, thus, have been constrained to institute suit for declaration as well as for partition. 

 4. First-third-defendants laid written statements controvert averments made in plaint. Defendants in written statement denied right, title and interest of plaintiffs over suit property. Defendants put forth pedigree contrary to case projected in plaint. It has been asserted that Mon Mohan Mondal died leaving behind only son Tufani Mondal and Tufani Mondal transferred entire inherited property in favour of Taizuddin by a deed of conveyance dated 14-1-1970. Taizuddin died leaving behind three sons first-third defendants and three daughters nineth-eleventh defendants and they have been exercising acts of possession on Suit property. First-third Defendants put up their ownership in respect of entire 'ka' and 'kha' schedule property. 

 6. Suit was taken up for preemptory hearing. Plaintiffs in support of their case examined three witnesses. First-third defendants, though, laid written-statement did not contest plaintiff's claim during trial and did not place on witness box any witness in support of contentions pressed into service in Written statement. 

 It is well settled principle of law regarding cross-examination that on failure of a party to cross-examine the witness of his adversary appearing against him on material evidence it will be presumed by Court that testimony given by that witness-in-chief has been accepted as it cannot be suggested that his statement on a particular fact is untrue unless he is cross-examined drawing his attention to that fact and thereby giving him an opportunity to explain the same. This rule of cross-examination is not merely "a technical rule of evidence" but it is as well "a rule of essential Justice" because it is essential to fair play and fair dealing with witnesses. In the said case the authoritative observation of Lord Chancellor Herschell in the case of Browne vs Dunn (1983) 6. R 67 has been quoted which is in the following language : 

 16. Learned Appellate Judge as last and final Judge of fact, though, was required to discuss and consider evidence of PWs 1, 2 and 3 in true perspective in the matter of coming to a just decision did not discuss and consider accounts supplied by PWs 1, 2 and 3 in right direction and, thus, committed a serious error in finding that statement of PW 1 was not supported by PWs 2 and 3 and by this error a failure of justice has been occasioned to plaintiffs-petitioners. 

 17. First-third defendants did not substantiate their case set out in written statement by examining themselves and other witnesses and their case was not at all required to be taken into consideration. Learned Appellate Judge positively held that defendants who filed written statement ultimately refrained from contesting the suit and defendants neither cross-examined PWs nor produced any independent evidence in support of defence contention. Learned Appellate Judge again held that defendants did not contest the suit and defendants, though, filed written statement did not substantiate it before Trial Judge. Learned Appellate Judge, thereafter, came to finding that learned Trial Judge committed serious illegality in considering defendant's case in his impugned judgment. In the face of positive findings arrived at by Learned Appellate Judge, he was required to reverse the decisions of Trial Judge and Learned Appellate Judge, thus, committed a grave error whereby a failure of justice has been occasioned. 

 20. Learned Trial Judge exhibited two deeds of conveyance dated 13-1-1970 and 14-1-1970 in favour of Taizuddin, predecessor of first-Third defendants and the two documents had been exhibited as Exhibits I and II. These two documents are not original deeds but simply photocopies of deeds. These two deeds, Exhibits I and II had not been at all admitted in evidence and exhibited in accordance with provisions of Evidence Act. None of defendants nor any witness came forward to stand on witness box in proof of the said two documents. Learned Trial Judge out of his own initiative and sun motu exhibited the said two deeds of conveyances as Exhibits I and II. Documents which are not copies of Judicial record should not be received in evidence without proof of signatures and hand writing of persons alleged to have signed or written them, even if such documents are brought on record and exhibited without objection. Soya Rani Guha alias Soya Rani Gupta vs Abdul Awal Mia and others, 47 DLR (AD) 45 orginal Kabala deed was not produced before Court and only certified copy of deed had been produced and the said deed was not proved in accordance with provisions of Evidence Act. It has been laid down that production of a certified copy of a sale deed does not, however, warrant presumption of due execution of original document and a party producing secondary evidence of a document is not relieved of the duty of proving execution of orginal. It has been further stated that even in a case where a document is exhibited without objection Court is to be satisfied as to execution of the document. In Atul Gomez and others vs Julian Rozario and others 6 MLR (AD) 46 original kabala deed was not produced in Court and certified copy of deed was admitted in evidence and marked as Exhibit. It has been held that unless a document is proved in accordance with law such document cannot be admitted in evidence and mere filing of the document is not sufficient to satisfy the requirement of law. In the case in hand, neither the original deed nor certified copy of two documents had been produced and only photocopies of the deeds had been in the record. Having given my anxious thought and consideration in respect of admissibility of the two documents, exhibited as Exhibit I and II and taking stock of Judicial authorities I am of this considered view that two deeds had been illegally exhibited by learned Trial Judge and decision reached by learned Trial Judge on the basis of Exhibits I and II are liable to be quashed and Exhibit I and II are left out of consideration in adjudicating claim of first-Third defendants. 

 21. Learned Trial Judge found plaintiff's suit to be barred by limitation adopting view that plaintiffs became aware of sale deeds of 1970 in the name of predecessors of first-third defendants and cloud had been cast on title over suit property during that period. Plaintiff laid suit for declaration of title on suit property and as well as for decree of partition. In paragraph No. 13 of plaint it has been stated that cause of action accrued on 25-4-1995 when first-seventh defendants denied title of plaintiff on suit property and, also, refused to effect partition. Paragraph No. 13 is extracted hereunder. 

 23. Learned Counsel for plaintiffs-petitioners and defendant-opposite parties candidly submitted that Revisional Settlement Khatian No. 1363 is in no way connected with suit property and Revisional Settlement Kha-tian No. 1363 had been wrongly and illegally brought in 'Ka' schedule property. Recorded owners of Revisional Settlement Khatian No. 1363 were not at all required to be impleaded as defendants in the suit. It can profitably be stated here that plaint had been drafted by a Muffosil Lawyer. Revisional Settlement Khatian No. 1363 had been inserted in 'Ka' schedule property by way of mistake and this mistake was committed by drafting Lawyer. It was been well settled through catena of Judicial autorities of Apex Courts that Muffosil Court's pleadings should be construed liberally and for confused pleadings, parties should not suffer. Md Zahoor Ali Khan 11 MIA (PC) 468 (Manng) Kyi Oh and another vs Ma Thet Pon AIR 1926(PC) 29, Manmatha Nath Kuri vs Moulavi Muhammad Muklesur Rahman and others PLD SC 565, Brindaban Chandra Chowdhury and another vs Musammat Rezia Begum and another 16 DLR 77, Managing Committee NMC Model High. School and others vs Obaidur Rahman Chowdhury and others 31 DLR (AD) 133 (134)are referred to in this regard. 

 24. Learned Appellate Judge in discarding claim of heir ship of predecessor of plaintiff’s Kailash Chandra Mondal from Ram Nath Mondal relied upon Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 1142. This Cadastral Survey Khatian had been exhibited as Exhibit A by learned Appellate Judge during appellate stage. Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 1142 was not exhibited in accordance with law and it was not admitted by Appellate Judge as an additional evidence under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code. Defendants-opposite parties did not at all make endeavor to have this Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 1142 exhibited as an additional evidence by way of a Petition under Order XLI, rule 27 of the Code. None from defendants-opposite parties stood on witness box in Appellate Court in proof of the said Cadastral Survey Khatian. Learned Appellate Judge, thus, committed a serious error in exhibiting Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 1142 as Exhibit-A. Moreover, no evidence had been led in support of recording in Cadastral Survey Khatian that Ramprashad Mondal was father of Kailash Chandra Mondal and Ram Nath Mondal was not father of Kailash Chandra Mondal. Learned Appellate Judge, thus, committed a substantial error in discarding the claim and heirship of Kailash Chandra Mondal from his father Ram Nath Mondal putting reliance upon Cadastral Survey Khatian No. 1142. It is posited here that learned Appellate Judge wrongly noted Exhibit-A as Exhibit 1 and this is, also, a demonstration of non-application of mind on the part of learned Appellate Judge. Learned Appellate Judge misread and misconstrued remarks column "jote Mono Mohan Mondal Raiyat Sthithiban জোত মনমোহন মন্ডল রায়ত স্থিতিবান in Cadastral Survey Khatian Nos. 1142 and by this misreading and misconstruction the merit of decision of appeal in respect of acquisition of interest on the part of Kailash Chandra Mondal on suit property had been materially affected causing thereby a grave injustice to plaintiffs-petitioners. 

 27. Cadastral survey record-of-right, though, is the oldest record-of-right prepared under section 103 of The Bengal Tenancy Act State Acquisition record-of-right being a latter record-of-right got presumptive value as to its correctness as enjoined under section 144A of The State Acquisition and Tenancy Act which enjoins that every entry in a record-of-right prepared or revised under section 144 shall be evidence of the matter referred to in such entry, and shall be presumed to be correct until it is proved by evidence to be incorrect. State Acquisition Record-of Right stands in the name of Kailash Chandra Mondal and Record-of-Right prepared in the name of Kailash Chandra Mondal, predecessor-father of plaintiffs-petitioners got presumptive value as to its correctness, of course, the presumption is rebut table one. Presumption of correctness in respect of Record-of-Right prepared in the name of Kailash Chandra Mondal, predecessor father of plaintiffs-petitioners had not been at all rebutted by first-Third defendants-opposite parties on producing reputable evidence. In the event of conflict between old record-of-right and recent record-of-right, recent record-of-right would prevail, inasmuch as presumption of record-of-right loses its weight with passage of time and entry in subsequent record-of-right would be more acceptable than earlier record-of-right. Support for the proposition is sought to be drawn from Bhupendra Krishna Ghose vs Abdur Rahman and others 61 CLL 18 and Abdul Hamid and others vs Abul Hossain Mir being dead his heirs Abdus Sobhan Mir and others 35 DLR 295.
